info.description: A fretboard diagram (guitar or bass). mode=theory stores musical parameters and computes dots at render; mode=explicit stores hand-placed dots. Position-addressed (string/fret) — keyboard diagrams use lesson.keyboard-diagram instead, which is pitch-class-addressed. Every field that can be an enum is one: a closed set is impossible for an LLM to get wrong under JSON-mode decoding, where a freeform array is not.

intent.description: What the diagram is OF, when mode=theory. Each intent is realized by @music-kb/music — the author says what to show, the theory layer decides where the dots go. chord: triadVoicing (root+quality+stringSet+inversion). scale: realizeCagedShape (root+scaleType+position). arpeggio: realizeArpeggio (root+quality+position). pattern: threeNotesPerString (root+scaleType+patternIndex). Absent means chord, which is what every diagram stored before intents existed is.

quality.description: Required for intent=chord and intent=arpeggio. intent=chord voices a triad, so only major/minor/augmented/diminished (or their short spellings maj/min/aug/dim) can be used there. intent=arpeggio accepts every value here — the list is exactly the qualities @music-kb/music has an arpeggio shape for (four distinct tones or fewer; a 9th/11th/13th lights up half a hand position and stops being an arpeggio picture).

stringSet.description: Required when mode=theory and intent=chord — which three strings voice the triad (resolveDiagramDots returns [] without it). Not used by the scale/arpeggio/pattern intents, and not used at all when mode=explicit.

scaleType.description: Required for intent=scale and intent=pattern. The @music-kb/music scale vocabulary, verbatim.

position.description: Required for intent=scale and intent=arpeggio: which hand position on the neck, the same vocabulary the scale boxes use. 1-5 are the numbered CAGED boxes; 2oct is the universal two-octave window anchored on the 6th-string root, which every scale and every arpeggio quality has. A string rather than an integer because 2oct is one of the values. NOT every combination is legal — majorPentatonic ships boxes 1 and 5 only, the modes ship none, and both authoring paths reject an illegal pair naming the legal values rather than rendering a blank neck.

patternIndex.description: Required for intent=pattern: which three-notes-per-string pattern, 1-based. Pattern N starts on scale degree N, so the legal maximum is the number of notes in the scale (7 for major and the modes, 6 for blues, 5 for the pentatonics) rather than a flat 7.
